text: 江苏的官方数据是再婚的平均年龄男40，女38，男的只比女的大2岁。
en: Jiangsu's official data shows that the average age at remarriage is 40 for men and 38 for women, with men only being two years older than women on average.

text: 如果40岁再婚男不考虑同龄女，那请问这些平均年龄38的再婚女是在和谁结婚?20岁小伙子?
en: If men seeking remarriage at 40 do not consider women of the same age, then may I ask whom these women remarrying at an average age of 38 are actually marrying? Twenty-year-old lads?

text: 另外一组数据是全省男比女大10岁以上的婚姻只有2%，光棍们不看数据整天拿强东和奶茶精神胜利法。
en: Another set of figures shows that across the whole province, only 2% of marriages involve a man more than ten years older than the woman. The bachelors, ignoring the data, clutch at Qiangdong and Milk Tea as a form of moral victory all day long.

text: 40岁女能看上的40岁男，几乎都能娶到年轻的。
en: The 40-year-old men that 40-year-old women actually fancy can, almost without exception, marry someone younger.

text: 40岁女看不上的40岁男，考虑也没用啊。
en: As for the 40-year-old men that 40-year-old women do not fancy, it is useless to even consider them.

text: 这些男的的想法没问题，有问题的是题主你。
en: These men's way of thinking is not the problem; the problem lies with you, the original poster.

text: 本题根本不是一个性别矛盾相关的话题，分析男性想法的，全部跑题了。
en: This question is fundamentally not a topic about gender conflict; everyone analysing men's thoughts has gone completely off topic.

text: 题主，你并没有弄明白你的定位，你是一个销售，你是一个乙方。
en: Original poster, you have not understood your position: you are a salesperson, you are Party B.

text: 相亲机构，也从来都不是公益匹配机构，本质上，还是销售集团居多。
en: Matchmaking agencies have never been public-welfare matching institutions either; essentially, they are mostly sales organisations.

text: 相亲机构销售的是什么呢？
en: What exactly do matchmaking agencies sell?

text: 是信息，通过介绍人的巧舌如簧，让会员们心甘情愿地为其他会员的信息买单。
en: They sell information; through the glib tongues of the matchmakers, they get members to willingly pay for the information about other members.

text: 那会员又为什么要报名你家的相亲机构呢？
en: Then why on earth do members sign up for your matchmaking agency?

text: 因为他们想要通过钱，去换取那些他们想要的信息。
en: Because they want to use money to obtain the information they desire.

text: 换言之，这就好像一个项目。
en: In other words, it is rather like a project.

text: 相亲会员是乙方，乙方给了你一笔钱（会费），然后跟你提出了定制需求（择偶条件）。
en: The matchmaking member is Party B; Party B gives you a sum of money (the membership fee) and then puts forward customised requirements (criteria for a partner).

text: 你的任务，就是找到信息（找到符合他们需求的对象），然后把信息落地（介绍成一对）。
en: Your task is to find the information (find an object that meets their needs) and then realise that information (introduce them as a couple).

text: 不可否认，确实有很多甲方的要求非常SB。
en: It cannot be denied that a great many Party A do put forward thoroughly idiotic requirements.

text: 但你有没有想过一个问题。
en: But have you ever considered a question.

text: 如果人家可以独立解决问题，人家又为什么要来你这里花钱呢？
en: If they could solve the problem on their own, then why would they come to you and spend money?

text: 人家跟你交会费，就是指望你能完成那些【他们无法独立完成，但希望你可以帮他们完成】的需求。
en: The very reason they pay you the membership fee is that they are counting on you to fulfil those requirements 【that they cannot fulfil on their own but hope you can help them fulfil】.

text: 所以才有很多人说嘛，能自由恋爱找到满意对象的，谁去相亲啊。
en: That is precisely why so many people say: whoever can find a satisfying partner through free dating would ever go to a matchmaker?

text: 你之所以觉得这些要求不合理，是因为你觉得完成难度过高成本过大，你搞不定。
en: The reason you find these demands unreasonable is that you think the difficulty and cost of fulfilling them are too high, and you cannot handle it.

text: 可是，这不代表，人家没有提要求的权利。
en: But that does not mean they have no right to make demands.

text: 更何况很多甲方，并不是真的SB，而是确实不够了解市场。
en: Moreover, many Party A are not actually being idiotic, but simply do not understand the market well enough.

text: 优秀的乙方，不仅可以让甲方有效了解市场情况，同时可以最大限度满足甲方的需求。
en: An excellent Party B can not only help Party A understand the market situation effectively, but also satisfy Party A's needs to the greatest extent.

text: 实际上，优秀的甲方的特点之一，本来就包括需求明确。
en: In fact, one of the characteristics of an excellent Party A is, by nature, having clear requirements.

text: 如果不确定自己的需求，又不够强势，反而容易被坑。
en: If you are unsure of your own needs and not assertive enough, you are instead easily taken advantage of.

text: 相亲市场之所以有大量的对人的打压，一个很重要的原因，就是婚恋销售们利用人们的婚恋焦虑，用贬低当事人价值的方式，逼迫对方妥协，从而实现【提高成交率】的效果。
en: One very important reason why the matchmaking market is full of so much undermining of people is that matchmaking salespeople exploit people's marriage-and-dating anxiety, using methods that belittle the person's worth to force them to compromise, thereby achieving the effect of 【raising the closing rate】.

text: 所以，年轻需求的成因或许没有人说得很清楚。
en: So perhaps no one has explained very clearly the cause of the demand for youth.

text: 但人家掏了钱，对着相亲机构，有没有资格提这个要求，当然有。
en: But having paid their money and facing the matchmaking agency, do they have the right to make this demand? Of course they do.

text: 从实然的角度，这些会员找不到年轻女宁可单身，也没什么问题啊。
en: From a de facto standpoint, there is nothing wrong with these members preferring to stay single rather than failing to find a young woman.

text: 因为找不到满足基本需求的对象——这是婚恋机构从业者，也就是题主你的问题啊。
en: Because they cannot find an object that meets their basic needs — that is the problem of us matchmaking practitioners, that is, you, the original poster.

text: 我自己就在珠宝行业晃荡，主要做设计，接触的基本都是消费不低，要求不少的人。
en: I myself have been drifting around in the jewellery industry, mainly doing design, and the people I deal with are basically those who spend quite a lot and have no shortage of demands.

text: 客观来说，好人不少，事儿逼也挺多。
en: Objectively speaking, there are quite a few good people, but also rather a lot of fussy, demanding sorts.

text: 所以实在受不了的时候，也免不了吐槽吐槽奇葩客户，亦或者吃吃客户的八卦。
en: So when I really cannot bear it, I cannot help but moan a little about oddball clients, or indeed dig into clients' gossip.

text: 这个在其他行业也比较普遍，毕竟大家多少都有过比较糟心的事儿。
en: This is fairly common in other industries too, after all everyone has had something rather annoying happen to them.

text: 就好像知乎的很多人会吃甲方的瓜，或者吐槽吐槽老板同事一样。
en: It is rather like how many people on Zhihu enjoy the gossip about their clients, or moan about their bosses and colleagues.

text: 但只有一种情况是一定会注意言行的：收了客户的钱之后，公开嫌弃客户钱少。
en: But there is only one situation in which one will certainly watch one's words and behaviour: after taking a client's money, openly looking down on the client for having little money.

text: 比如说之前有一个同行，嘲笑一个想要通过两万预算做结果珠宝三件套的客户没钱还痴人说梦，大家知道这件事情之后都觉得这个人不对。
en: For example, there was a colleague who mocked a client who wanted to have a finished three-piece jewellery set made on a budget of 20,000 yuan, saying the client was penniless yet dreaming impossible dreams; once everyone learnt of this, they all felt this person was in the wrong.

text: 原因很简单：
en: The reason is simple:

text: 按照人家的需求提供建议和方案，这不就是咱们专业搞的事情吗？
en: Providing suggestions and solutions according to the client's needs — is that not exactly what we professionals do?

text: 人家买的就是这个服务呀。
en: What the client is buying is precisely this service.

text: 有钱人的生意谁都会做，刷卡谁都会，这并不能体现出专业能力。
en: Anyone can do business with rich people, anyone can swipe a card; that does not demonstrate professional ability.

text: 如果觉得做不了，完全可以直接和客户商量，收钱的时候不含糊，然后背地里笑话人家钱不多，不太好吧？
en: If you feel you cannot do it, you can simply discuss it directly with the client; it is rather unfair to take the money without hesitation and then laugh at them behind their back for not having much, is it not?

text: 嫌弃利润少就别赚呀。
en: If you dislike the slim profit, then simply do not take the job.

text: 客户又没有在前面隐藏需求事后疯狂挑刺，人家一开始就把要求说得明明白白。
en: The client did not hide their needs up front and then pick faults madly afterwards; they spelled out the requirements clearly from the very beginning.

text: 两万块确实不多，但只要有心一点都不难。
en: 20,000 yuan truly is not much, but as long as one is willing, it is not difficult at all.

text: 简单经典的三件套，我随便想一下都能想出N多个方案，之前有小伙伴希望设计过类似预算的多件套，带主题带工艺，我也照样做出来了啊（摊手）
en: For a simple, classic three-piece set, I can think up N number of plans just off the top of my head; a colleague once hoped I would design a multi-piece set at a similar budget, with a theme and craftsmanship, and I delivered all the same (shrugs).

text: 相亲这个事儿也是同理。
en: Matchmaking works on the same principle.

text: 客户想要年轻的，又没说非得白富美，那年轻普女行不行，年轻穷女孩行不行？
en: The client wants someone young, but did not say it must be a fair, rich and beautiful woman — so would a young ordinary woman do, would a young poor girl do?

text: 相亲机构的优势啥？
en: What is the matchmaking agency's advantage, then?

text: 不就是不一定能谈到一起，但是总能给你找到满足你硬件需求的对象吗？
en: Is it not precisely that they may not always bring two people together, but can always find you an object that meets your hard criteria?

text: 更何况大机构的一对一相亲服务，价格一定是不便宜的。
en: Moreover, one-to-one matchmaking services at large agencies certainly do not come cheap.

text: 可能仅仅服务三五个月就要付出好几万。
en: Serving someone for just three to five months may cost tens of thousands.

text: 人家购买的是什么呢，购买的不就是公司的VIP人脉吗？
en: What is it that they are buying, if not the company's VIP network?

text: 看清楚诶，诸位，硬件，硬件。
en: See clearly, everyone — hard criteria, hard criteria.

text: 我知道奇葩客户很多，但是作为从业者，不管客户多么有问题，在没有真正伤害你之前，你都应该对客户抱有基本的尊重，这是涉及到任何一个行业都很基础的职业道德。
en: I know there are many oddball clients, but as a practitioner, no matter how problematic a client may be, before they truly harm you, you ought to hold a basic respect for the client; this is a most basic professional ethic that applies to any industry.

text: 题主你作为一个乙方，要求甲方又给你掏钱，还要为了让你省心去改需求，你在想什么屁吃？
en: Original poster, as Party B, you demand that Party A pay you and moreover change their requirements just to make things easier for you — what on earth are you dreaming of?

text: 最后安利一下本人的专栏，干货满满。
en: Finally, let me recommend my own column; it is packed with substance.

text: 我是 @非癯仙 欢迎关注点赞。
en: I am @Fei Quxian; welcome to follow and like.

text: 点个赞，同样是真诚地表达善意的方式。
en: Giving a like is likewise a sincere way of expressing goodwill.

text: 我得到了你的支持鼓励，会更加努力，然后产出更多优秀的内容回馈你。
en: Having received your support and encouragement, I will work harder and produce more excellent content to give back to you.

text: 欢迎关注本人的某书，情感内容以后都会放在这里~（老被抄，好烦，干脆自己开号）
en: Welcome to follow my Xiaohongshu; emotional-content posts will all be placed here from now on~ (always getting copied, so annoying, so I simply opened my own account).
